24: /// A queue of delayed elements.
25: ///
26: /// Once an element is inserted into the `DelayQueue`, it is yielded once the
27: /// specified deadline has been reached.
28: ///
29: /// # Usage
30: ///
31: /// Elements are inserted into `DelayQueue` using the [`insert`] or
32: /// [`insert_at`] methods. A deadline is provided with the item and a [`Key`] is
33: /// returned. The key is used to remove the entry or to change the deadline at
34: /// which it should be yielded back.
35: ///
36: /// Once delays have been configured, the `DelayQueue` is used via its
37: /// [`Stream`] implementation. [`poll_expired`] is called. If an entry has reached its
38: /// deadline, it is returned. If not, `Poll::Pending` is returned indicating that the
39: /// current task will be notified once the deadline has been reached.
40: ///
41: /// # `Stream` implementation
42: ///
43: /// Items are retrieved from the queue via [`DelayQueue::poll_expired`]. If no delays have
44: /// expired, no items are returned. In this case, `Poll::Pending` is returned and the
45: /// current task is registered to be notified once the next item's delay has
46: /// expired.
47: ///
48: /// If no items are in the queue, i.e. `is_empty()` returns `true`, then `poll`
49: /// returns `Poll::Ready(None)`. This indicates that the stream has reached an end.
50: /// However, if a new item is inserted *after*, `poll` will once again start
51: /// returning items or `Poll::Pending`.
52: ///
53: /// Items are returned ordered by their expirations. Items that are configured
54: /// to expire first will be returned first. There are no ordering guarantees
55: /// for items configured to expire at the same instant. Also note that delays are
56: /// rounded to the closest millisecond.
57: ///
58: /// # Implementation
59: ///
60: /// The [`DelayQueue`] is backed by a separate instance of a timer wheel similar to that used internally
61: /// by Tokio's standalone timer utilities such as [`sleep`]. Because of this, it offers the same
62: /// performance and scalability benefits.
63: ///
64: /// State associated with each entry is stored in a [`slab`]. This amortizes the cost of allocation,
65: /// and allows reuse of the memory allocated for expired entries.
66: ///
67: /// Capacity can be checked using [`capacity`] and allocated preemptively by using
68: /// the [`reserve`] method.
69: ///
70: /// # Usage
71: ///
72: /// Using `DelayQueue` to manage cache entries.
73: ///
74: /// ```rust,no_run
75: /// use tokio_util::time::{DelayQueue, delay_queue};
76: ///
77: /// use futures::ready;
78: /// use std::collections::HashMap;
79: /// use std::task::{Context, Poll};
80: /// use std::time::Duration;
81: /// # type CacheKey = String;
82: /// # type Value = String;
83: ///
84: /// struct Cache {
85: ///     entries: HashMap<CacheKey, (Value, delay_queue::Key)>,
86: ///     expirations: DelayQueue<CacheKey>,
87: /// }
88: ///
89: /// const TTL_SECS: u64 = 30;
90: ///
91: /// impl Cache {
92: ///     fn insert(&mut self, key: CacheKey, value: Value) {
93: ///         let delay = self.expirations
94: ///             .insert(key.clone(), Duration::from_secs(TTL_SECS));
95: ///
96: ///         self.entries.insert(key, (value, delay));
97: ///     }
98: ///
99: ///     fn get(&self, key: &CacheKey) -> Option<&Value> {
100: ///         self.entries.get(key)
101: ///             .map(|&(ref v, _)| v)
102: ///     }
103: ///
104: ///     fn remove(&mut self, key: &CacheKey) {
105: ///         if let Some((_, cache_key)) = self.entries.remove(key) {
106: ///             self.expirations.remove(&cache_key);
107: ///         }
108: ///     }
109: ///
110: ///     fn poll_purge(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<()> {
111: ///         while let Some(entry) = ready!(self.expirations.poll_expired(cx)) {
112: ///             self.entries.remove(entry.get_ref());
113: ///         }
114: ///
115: ///         Poll::Ready(())
116: ///     }
117: /// }
118: /// ```

121: /// [`insert_at`]: method@Self::insert_at

123: /// [`Stream`]: https://docs.rs/futures/0.1/futures/stream/trait.Stream.html
124: /// [`poll_expired`]: method@Self::poll_expired
125: /// [`Stream::poll_expired`]: method@Self::poll_expired

159: struct SlabStorage<T> {
160:     inner: Slab<Data<T>>,
161: 
162:     // A `compact` call requires a re-mapping of the `Key`s that were changed
163:     // during the `compact` call of the `slab`. Since the keys that were given out
164:     // cannot be changed retroactively we need to keep track of these re-mappings.
165:     // The keys of `key_map` correspond to the old keys that were given out and
166:     // the values to the `Key`s that were re-mapped by the `compact` call.
167:     key_map: HashMap<Key, KeyInternal>,
168: 
169:     // Index used to create new keys to hand out.
170:     next_key_index: usize,
171: 
172:     // Whether `compact` has been called, necessary in order to decide whether
173:     // to include keys in `key_map`.
174:     compact_called: bool,
175: }

177: impl<T> SlabStorage<T> {
178:     pub(crate) fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> SlabStorage<T> {
179:         SlabStorage {
180:             inner: Slab::with_capacity(capacity),
181:             key_map: HashMap::new(),
182:             next_key_index: 0,
183:             compact_called: false,
184:         }
185:     }
186: 
187:     // Inserts data into the inner slab and re-maps keys if necessary
188:     pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, val: Data<T>) -> Key {
189:         let mut key = KeyInternal::new(self.inner.insert(val));
190:         let key_contained = self.key_map.contains_key(&key.into());
191: 
192:         if key_contained {
193:             // It's possible that a `compact` call creates capacity in `self.inner` in
194:             // such a way that a `self.inner.insert` call creates a `key` which was
195:             // previously given out during an `insert` call prior to the `compact` call.
196:             // If `key` is contained in `self.key_map`, we have encountered this exact situation,
197:             // We need to create a new key `key_to_give_out` and include the relation
198:             // `key_to_give_out` -> `key` in `self.key_map`.
199:             let key_to_give_out = self.create_new_key();
200:             assert!(!self.key_map.contains_key(&key_to_give_out.into()));
201:             self.key_map.insert(key_to_give_out.into(), key);
202:             key = key_to_give_out;
203:         } else if self.compact_called {
204:             // Include an identity mapping in `self.key_map` in order to allow us to
205:             // panic if a key that was handed out is removed more than once.
206:             self.key_map.insert(key.into(), key);
207:         }
208: 
209:         key.into()
210:     }
211: 
212:     // Re-map the key in case compact was previously called.
213:     // Note: Since we include identity mappings in key_map after compact was called,
214:     // we have information about all keys that were handed out. In the case in which
215:     // compact was called and we try to remove a Key that was previously removed
216:     // we can detect invalid keys if no key is found in `key_map`. This is necessary
217:     // in order to prevent situations in which a previously removed key
218:     // corresponds to a re-mapped key internally and which would then be incorrectly
219:     // removed from the slab.
220:     //
221:     // Example to illuminate this problem:
222:     //
223:     // Let's assume our `key_map` is {1 -> 2, 2 -> 1} and we call remove(1). If we
224:     // were to remove 1 again, we would not find it inside `key_map` anymore.
225:     // If we were to imply from this that no re-mapping was necessary, we would
226:     // incorrectly remove 1 from `self.slab.inner`, which corresponds to the
227:     // handed-out key 2.
228:     pub(crate) fn remove(&mut self, key: &Key) -> Data<T> {
229:         let remapped_key = if self.compact_called {
230:             match self.key_map.remove(key) {
231:                 Some(key_internal) => key_internal,
232:                 None => panic!("invalid key"),
233:             }
234:         } else {
235:             (*key).into()
236:         };
237: 
238:         self.inner.remove(remapped_key.index)
239:     }
240: 
241:     fn remove_internal(&mut self, key: KeyInternal) -> Data<T> {
242:         self.inner.remove(key.index)
243:     }
244: 
245:     pub(crate) fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {
246:         self.inner.shrink_to_fit();
247:         self.key_map.shrink_to_fit();
248:     }
249: 
250:     pub(crate) fn compact(&mut self) {
251:         if !self.compact_called {
252:             for (key, _) in self.inner.iter() {
253:                 self.key_map.insert(Key::new(key), KeyInternal::new(key));
254:             }
255:         }
256: 
257:         let mut remapping = HashMap::new();
258:         self.inner.compact(|_, from, to| {
259:             remapping.insert(from, to);
260:             true
261:         });
262: 
263:         // At this point `key_map` contains a mapping for every element.
264:         for internal_key in self.key_map.values_mut() {
265:             if let Some(new_internal_key) = remapping.get(&internal_key.index) {
266:                 *internal_key = KeyInternal::new(*new_internal_key);
267:             }
268:         }
269: 
270:         if self.key_map.capacity() > 2 * self.key_map.len() {
271:             self.key_map.shrink_to_fit();
272:         }
273: 
274:         self.compact_called = true;
275:     }
276: 
277:     // Tries to re-map a `Key` that was given out to the user to its
278:     // corresponding internal key.
279:     fn remap_key(&self, key: &Key) -> Option<KeyInternal> {
280:         let key_map = &self.key_map;
281:         if self.compact_called {
282:             key_map.get(key).copied()
283:         } else {
284:             Some((*key).into())
285:         }
286:     }
287: 
288:     fn create_new_key(&mut self) -> KeyInternal {
289:         while self.key_map.contains_key(&Key::new(self.next_key_index)) {
290:             self.next_key_index = self.next_key_index.wrapping_add(1);
291:         }
292: 
293:         KeyInternal::new(self.next_key_index)
294:     }
295: 
296:     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
297:         self.inner.len()
298:     }
299: 
300:     pub(crate) fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
301:         self.inner.capacity()
302:     }
303: 
304:     pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
305:         self.inner.clear();
306:         self.key_map.clear();
307:         self.compact_called = false;
308:     }
309: 
310:     pub(crate) fn reserve(&mut self, additional: usize) {
311:         self.inner.reserve(additional);
312: 
313:         if self.compact_called {
314:             self.key_map.reserve(additional);
315:         }
316:     }
317: 
318:     pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
319:         self.inner.is_empty()
320:     }
321: 
322:     pub(crate) fn contains(&self, key: &Key) -> bool {
323:         let remapped_key = self.remap_key(key);
324: 
325:         match remapped_key {
326:             Some(internal_key) => self.inner.contains(internal_key.index),
327:             None => false,
328:         }
329:     }
330: }

446:     /// # use tokio_util::time::DelayQueue;

479:         DelayQueue {
480:             wheel: Wheel::new(),
481:             slab: SlabStorage::with_capacity(capacity),
482:             expired: Stack::default(),
483:             delay: None,
484:             wheel_now: 0,
485:             start: Instant::now(),
486:             waker: None,

490:     /// Inserts `value` into the queue set to expire at a specific instant in
491:     /// time.
492:     ///
493:     /// This function is identical to `insert`, but takes an `Instant` instead
494:     /// of a `Duration`.
495:     ///
496:     /// `value` is stored in the queue until `when` is reached. At which point,
497:     /// `value` will be returned from [`poll_expired`]. If `when` has already been
498:     /// reached, then `value` is immediately made available to poll.
499:     ///
500:     /// The return value represents the insertion and is used as an argument to
501:     /// [`remove`] and [`reset`]. Note that [`Key`] is a token and is reused once
502:     /// `value` is removed from the queue either by calling [`poll_expired`] after
503:     /// `when` is reached or by calling [`remove`]. At this point, the caller
504:     /// must take care to not use the returned [`Key`] again as it may reference
505:     /// a different item in the queue.
506:     ///
507:     /// See [type] level documentation for more details.
508:     ///
509:     /// # Panics
510:     ///
511:     /// This function panics if `when` is too far in the future.
512:     ///
513:     /// # Examples
514:     ///
515:     /// Basic usage
516:     ///
517:     /// ```rust
518:     /// use tokio::time::{Duration, Instant};
519:     /// use tokio_util::time::DelayQueue;
520:     ///
521:     /// # #[tokio::main]
522:     /// # async fn main() {
523:     /// let mut delay_queue = DelayQueue::new();
524:     /// let key = delay_queue.insert_at(
525:     ///     "foo", Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5));
526:     ///
527:     /// // Remove the entry
528:     /// let item = delay_queue.remove(&key);
529:     /// assert_eq!(*item.get_ref(), "foo");
530:     /// # }
531:     /// ```
532:     ///
533:     /// [`poll_expired`]: method@Self::poll_expired
534:     /// [`remove`]: method@Self::remove
535:     /// [`reset`]: method@Self::reset
536:     /// [`Key`]: struct@Key
537:     /// [type]: #
538:     #[track_caller]
539:     pub fn insert_at(&mut self, value: T, when: Instant) -> Key {
540:         assert!(self.slab.len() < MAX_ENTRIES, "max entries exceeded");
541: 
542:         // Normalize the deadline. Values cannot be set to expire in the past.
543:         let when = self.normalize_deadline(when);
544: 
545:         // Insert the value in the store
546:         let key = self.slab.insert(Data {
547:             inner: value,
548:             when,
549:             expired: false,
550:             next: None,
551:             prev: None,
552:         });
553: 
554:         self.insert_idx(when, key);
555: 
556:         // Set a new delay if the current's deadline is later than the one of the new item
557:         let should_set_delay = if let Some(ref delay) = self.delay {
558:             let current_exp = self.normalize_deadline(delay.deadline());
559:             current_exp > when
560:         } else {
561:             true
562:         };
563: 
564:         if should_set_delay {
565:             if let Some(waker) = self.waker.take() {
566:                 waker.wake();
567:             }
568: 
569:             let delay_time = self.start + Duration::from_millis(when);
570:             if let Some(ref mut delay) = &mut self.delay {
571:                 delay.as_mut().reset(delay_time);
572:             } else {
573:                 self.delay = Some(Box::pin(sleep_until(delay_time)));
574:             }
575:         }

578:     }

580:     /// Attempts to pull out the next value of the delay queue, registering the
581:     /// current task for wakeup if the value is not yet available, and returning
582:     /// `None` if the queue is exhausted.
583:     pub fn poll_expired(&mut self, cx: &mut task::Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Expired<T>>> {
584:         if !self
585:             .waker
586:             .as_ref()
587:             .map(|w| w.will_wake(cx.waker()))
588:             .unwrap_or(false)
589:         {
590:             self.waker = Some(cx.waker().clone());
591:         }
592: 
593:         let item = ready!(self.poll_idx(cx));
594:         Poll::Ready(item.map(|key| {
595:             let data = self.slab.remove(&key);
596:             debug_assert!(data.next.is_none());
597:             debug_assert!(data.prev.is_none());
598: 
599:             Expired {
600:                 key,
601:                 data: data.inner,
602:                 deadline: self.start + Duration::from_millis(data.when),
603:             }
604:         }))
605:     }

623:     /// use the returned [`Key`] again as it may reference a different
624:     /// item in the queue.

1121:     /// should be returned.

1123:     /// A slot should be returned when the associated deadline has been reached.

1125:         use self::wheel::Stack;

1127:         let expired = self.expired.pop(&mut self.slab);
1128: 
1129:         if expired.is_some() {
1130:             return Poll::Ready(expired);
1131:         }
1132: 
1133:         loop {
1134:             if let Some(ref mut delay) = self.delay {
1135:                 if !delay.is_elapsed() {
1136:                     ready!(Pin::new(&mut *delay).poll(cx));
1137:                 }
1138: 
1139:                 let now = crate::time::ms(delay.deadline() - self.start, crate::time::Round::Down);
1140: 
1141:                 self.wheel_now = now;
1142:             }
1143: 
1144:             // We poll the wheel to get the next value out before finding the next deadline.
1145:             let wheel_idx = self.wheel.poll(self.wheel_now, &mut self.slab);
1146: 
1147:             self.delay = self.next_deadline().map(|when| Box::pin(sleep_until(when)));
1148: 
1149:             if let Some(idx) = wheel_idx {
1150:                 return Poll::Ready(Some(idx));
1151:             }

1153:             if self.delay.is_none() {
1154:                 return Poll::Ready(None);
1155:             }
